title: Coalesced inference advisor: workload-shape profiler and safe config apply
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build an advisor service that recommends coalesced/continuous batching and cache parameters per workload while providing automated, auditable safe-apply and rollback for production inference pools.

Why: Many customers have heterogeneous request shapes (short chat turns + occasional long completions). Static batch/caching configs either waste GPU cycles or violate latency SLOs. An advisor that profiles workload shape and proposes conservative, safety-checked config changes can reduce token cost by ~10-30% while keeping p95 latency within SLO.

Scope:
- Offline and streaming workload profiler capturing request size percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99 token lengths), session grouping patterns, arrival clustering, and KV cache hit/eviction statistics.
- Heuristics engine that synthesizes recommendations for: max_batch_ms (coalescing window), target_tokens_per_batch, max_batch_size, prefix_cache_enabled, kv_cache_ttl_seconds, per-model quantized fallback pairs.
- Scorecard: cost delta estimate, expected p95 latency delta, safety margin, confidence score.
- Safe apply path: staged rollout (canary -> ramp), automated validation checks and automatic rollback triggers based on guardrails (latency regression, error spike, cost drift).
- Operator UI hooks in Console: preview diff, estimated cost savings, rollout controls, audit trail, and manual rollback.

Design notes / heuristics summary:
- Workload fingerprinting: cluster request traces by shape vector [tokens_in, tokens_out, is_stream, session_id_entropy]. Use lightweight LSH for online bucketing to avoid heavy clustering jobs.
- Recommendation policy: pick conservative proposal where predicted p95 latency <= SLO + 10% and confidence >= 70%. If multiple fingerprints exist, propose per-route config or an aggregate config with per-fingerprint overrides.
- Continuous batching parameters: prefer small increases to max_batch_ms (10ms -> 20ms) when arrival rate low, aggressive target_tokens_per_batch when steady-state token throughput is high.
- KV cache interplay: if prefix cache hit_rate > 50% and evictions low, enable prefix_cache_enabled and raise kv_cache_ttl_seconds. Conversely, if cache churn high, recommend smaller batches to reduce working-set pressure.
- Cost model: amortize fixed GPU kernel overhead with expected tokens/batch; apply conservative penalties for quantized models where quality regressions could occur.

Safe apply and rollback:
- Rollout plan: canary (1%) for 2h -> 10% for 12h -> 50% for 24h -> full. At each step run validation suite: p95 latency, error rate, token-per-request cost.
- Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 12% above baseline, error rate > baseline + 0.4%, cost > predicted + 15%, or manual abort.
- Atomicity: configuration changes must be applied atomically per serving-pool to avoid heterogeneous behavior within a single request stream. This requires the runtime to support versioned config pins (work in progress with infra team).
- Observability: record before/after histograms for latency, token counts, KV hit rates, and cost. Store diffs in Console for 90 days.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Profiler agent (v1): lightweight streaming collector that emits aggregated fingerprints per 5m window. (Owner: Marcus)
2) Offline recommender prototype: run on past 30d traces to validate model and heuristics. (Owner: Sophie)
3) Safe-apply controller: feature-flagged service in control plane to orchestrate staged rollout and monitor metrics (Owner: Diego).
4) Console integration: UI preview, rollout controls, audit log. (Owner: Nisha)
5) Pilot with two internal test customers and one low-traffic external customer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Profiler emits stable fingerprints for ≥90% of traffic with <1% ingestion overhead.
- Recommender proposals pass synthetic replay tests: predicted cost reduction within ±15% of observed and p95 latency within SLO + 10%.
- Safe-apply controller can perform a 1% -> 10% canary ramp with rollback on trigger within 15 minutes.

Risks & open questions:
- Runtime support for atomic config pins across GPU processes (blocked on infra ticket ENG-100240).
- Quality regressions when recommending quantized fallbacks for certain models—need eval set per customer.
- Multi-tenant vs dedicated pools: recommend per-customer defaults only when we can reliably isolate metrics.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/CIA-Advisor-Proposal
- Prototype PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5281
- Cost modelling notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qCostModelNotebook

Next steps (this cycle):
- Deliver profiler v1 alpha and run offline recommender on last 14 days of traces.
- Align with infra on atomic config apply and finalize automated rollback thresholds.
